objects.original: Initialized sphere-valued Ito rows, field values u_t, temperature and a zero-start martingale.
objects.reconstructed: Put d=card(I), c=real(max(d-1,0)) (natural-number subtraction before casting), E=R^I with Euclidean norm, S={x in E: ||x||=1}, V_j(x)=e_j-x_j*x, and L_S f(x)=Laplacian(f)(x)-D^2 f(x)[x,x]-c*Df(x)[x]. Here Df is the Frechet derivative and D^2 f=D(Df). Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Define A_i(t,omega)=x_i(omega)+integral_0^t b_i(s,omega)ds and X(t,omega)=(A_i(t,omega)+sum_j I_T^j(eta_ij)(t,omega))_i. The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereItoIntegratedRows.lean:17; x,b,eta build the literal initialized rows and same Brownian-coordinate integrals.

domains.original: Finite measure, finite Euclidean sphere with a supplied point, T>0.
domains.reconstructed: Omega measurable, I finite with decidable equality, mu a finite measure, filtration on R_+, T>0, B:R_+ x Omega->E. eta:I x I->ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); x:Omega->R^I; b:I x R_+ x Omega->R; fallback in S; f:E->R; u:R_+ x Omega->E; a:R_+->R.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereItoIntegratedRows.lean:17; fallback supplies an actual unit vector, so dimension is nonzero and natural card−1 agrees with usual d−1.

quantifiers.original: After the three a.e. all-horizon range/drift/diffusion premises, there exists M with terminal identity.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally the spaces, instances, filtration,mu,T,B, hB,hT,hUsual,eta,x,hx,b,hb,hbi,fallback,f,hf,u,a,hNonneg. Then three implications, respectively sphere membership, drift identity, diffusion-column identities. After all three premises there exists a real process M on R_+ x Omega.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereItoIntegratedRows.lean:17; The three implication premises are a.e. simultaneously for all t≤T (and all j for diffusion); M is chosen afterwards.

assumptions.original: F_0-measurable initials; progressive pathwise-integrable drift; progressive product-L² noise; nonnegative temperature; ambient C² test and usual Brownian setup.
assumptions.reconstructed: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). Each x_i is strongly measurable with respect to filtration(0), b_i strongly progressive, and b_i(.,omega) is lambda_T-integrable for mu-a.e. omega. f is C^2 at every sphere point, a(t)>=0 for every t<=T, and fallback is an actual sphere point. Assume mu-a.e. omega, for every t<=T, X(t,omega) belongs to S; assume mu-a.e. omega, for every t<=T, b(t,omega)=-u(t,omega)-a(t)*c*X(t,omega); assume mu-a.e. omega, for every t<=T and j, eta_.j(t,omega)=sqrt(2*a(t))*V_j(X(t,omega)). No explicit continuity or measurability assumption on u or a is listed beyond these statements.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereItoIntegratedRows.lean:17; Unlike the stronger continuous-temperature wrapper, this target has no hu or hTemperature binder; none is silently added.

conclusion.original: Terminal increment equals integral of -Df[u]+temperature times sphere Laplacian plus M_T.
conclusion.reconstructed: There exists a filtration-martingale M with respect to mu, M(0,omega)=0 for every omega, and for mu-a.e. omega: f(X(T,omega))-f(X(0,omega))=integral_0^T [-Df(X(s,omega))[u(s,omega)]+a(s)*L_S f(X(s,omega))]ds+M(T,omega).
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereItoIntegratedRows.lean:17; On the unit sphere sum_hessian_projectedNoiseColumn identifies the source projected trace with the definition Delta f−D²f[w,w]; the radial term and half-noise square give the source generator.

scopes.original: Terminal a.e. identity; M true martingale globally and M_0 pointwise zero.
scopes.reconstructed: The martingale assertion is for the whole R_+-indexed M, while the displayed decomposition is asserted only at terminal time T. Zero initial value is pointwise for all omega. Three premises hold a.e. uniformly over the fixed horizon. The measure is finite, not separately required to be a probability measure.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/SphereItoIntegratedRows.lean:17; The target asserts only f(X_T)−f(X_0), although M is defined for all nonnegative times.
